question.problem: Given the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}]$, find a basis of $\text{Null}(A).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce the matrix $A$ to reduced row echelon form (RREF):

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -2 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 5 & -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So, equation $Ax=0$ is equivalent to the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{3}+2{x}_{4}=0 \\ {x}_{2}+5{x}_{3}-{x}_{4}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

The general solution is ${x}_{1}=2{x}_{3}-2{x}_{4}$ and ${x}_{2}=-5{x}_{3}+{x}_{4},$ where ${x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are free variables. Therefore, if $x\in \text{Null}(A),$ then

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3}-2{x}_{4} \\ -5{x}_{3}+{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{3} \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2{x}_{3} \\ -5{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-2{x}_{4} \\ {x}_{4} \\ 0 \\ {x}_{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & ={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{4}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3},{x}_{4}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

This implies that 

$$
B=\{[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\}
$$

is a basis of $\text{Null}(A)$ since it is a linearly independent set and its vectors generate $\text{Null}(A).$
